Exp 572 · paper 217 · assessment v324 · script ResearchOutput/scripts/2026-08-24-round74/exp572_ma1_signed.py · seed 572 · wall 6.96 s.

**Question.** Paper 213/exp566 closed the MAGNITUDE route of MA-1 effectivity (|L(1,χ)| does not predict |AP deviations|, R²=0.019) but preserved the SIGNED route: do signs of character-twisted prime-count deviations align with signs predicted by computable character data? A yes would be the first computable handle on AP-deviation structure.

**Key structural disclosure** (post-smoke, pre-full-data): L(1,χ)>0 for EVERY real non-principal χ (class-number formula) ⇒ sign(w)≡+1 identically (n_cells_w_negative=0 at full scale), so registered criterion C1 reduces exactly to Pr[c_χ>0] and could only fire if prime twists were majority-positive. Working identity asserted exact (<1e-9): c_χ = Σ_a d_a·χ(a) = Σ_{p≤x} χ(p); the uniform-li theory term vanishes identically by orthogonality, so signed L(1,χ) is the only computable x-independent theory weight.

**Design.** x=2²⁶ full (π(x)=3,957,809); 287 moduli (squarefree [3,300] ∪ primes [307,997]); 491 real-char cells; 86,882 unit classes; machinery verbatim from exp566 (class-number exact D<0 |D|≤400, truncated-L otherwise, median rel err 1.8e-5); CP95 intervals + within-modulus d-shuffle null (2000 draws — MEANINGFUL here unlike exp566 since sign(c) is not permutation-invariant in a).

**Result H0 — both criteria fail, both levels.** Cell agreement 15.07% over 491 cells (74 agree), CP95 [0.1202, 0.1855], circular-sum z=−52.72 (C2 needs >3). Class level 48.74% over 86,882 classes, CP95 [0.4841, 0.4907], permutation z=−7.74 — significantly BELOW chance (mild anti-alignment). Breakdowns all CIs wholly below 50%: prime-modulus quadratics 26.9% (167), product chars ω≥2 8.95% (324), exact-L 12.8% (226), truncated-L 17.0% (265), drop-|w|<1e-3 robustness unchanged.

**Named byproduct** (labeled exploratory, not pre-registered): prime twists NEGATIVE in 84.7% of cells (CP95 [0.8123, 0.8779]; smoke x=2²² read 91.7%) — the universal Chebyshev/Rubinstein–Sarnak low bias, independently confirmed inside the lab's own AP-deviation machinery at x=2²⁶. Deviation signs are one-directional across moduli and zero-driven, NOT carried by any computable L-value — precisely why no L-based predictor can track them.

**Ledger.** (1) m=6 orthogonality assert exposed the raw-primitive-twist ±1 correction for primes p|m, p∤cond(χ) (max corr 3, 0 sign flips induced — disclosed, not corrected); (2) class-z scale mix-up fixed (−310 → single-scale −7.74); (3) exp566's 'within-modulus shuffle vacuous' caveat verified NOT to transfer here.

**Barrier framing.** Closes barrier-map residual 'MA-1 effectivity' as a named question: no computable criterion via quadratic-character structure on either route (magnitude paper 213, sign here) at toy scale; the averaging identity's effective scope remains non-computable from N; consistent with barriers 4/5. No breakthrough.

concept.title: Efficiency Gap as an Information Lower Bound
concept.concept_description:
With both ceilings known, define a statistic's efficiency as reading^2 divided by its tie ceiling. At bitlen 52 the dial has efficiency 0.58 and the count baseline 0.41. Conjecture that this efficiency gap lower-bounds the extra mutual information the 2-adic valuation carries about the response, via a Fano-type inequality for rank correlations.

For any response Y and statistics T, C on the same sample, eff(T) - eff(C) <= c * (I(T;Y) - I(C;Y)) for an absolute constant c, where eff denotes squared Spearman reading divided by tie ceiling.

Formalise efficiency in the existing tie-profile framework, prove the data-processing direction first (C a function of T implies eff(C) <= eff(T)), and calibrate c on the recorded bitlen-52 pair.

The dial's advantage becomes a certified information statement rather than a correlational one, and the validation band acquires an information-theoretic meaning.

Rank efficiency and mutual information are not comparable, so dial advantages must be reported strictly as rank statistics.
